html:
The Malécu, also called Guatuso, are a small Chibchan-speaking people of the plains of northern Costa Rica, near the Río Frío and the border with Nicaragua. Protected by dense forest, they kept apart from the Spanish for centuries.

In the late 1800s rubber tappers from Nicaragua raided them, killing many and selling captives, and their numbers fell to a few hundred. Today they live on a small reserve in Guatuso county and work to keep their language, Maléku Jaíka, alive. Their neighbours to the west were the Chorotega, and they are one of the Indigenous peoples of Costa Rica, with the Bribri and Huetar.
